name: the Orto Botanico di Padova
title: Ancient Trees in Padua's Botanical Garden: 5 Worth Finding
meta_description: The world's first university botanical garden, founded 1545, and the five remarkable trees still growing inside its UNESCO-listed walls.
intro: The University of Padua founded this garden in 1545 to teach medical students which plants their patients were actually being given, the first botanical garden anywhere attached to a university and the model every later one copied. UNESCO listed it as a World Heritage Site in 1997, citing its continuous four-and-a-half centuries of scientific use rather than its age alone. Five of the trees we map grow inside its circular walls, among them a dwarf palm Goethe wrote about, a ginkgo grafted to bear both pollen and fruit from one trunk, and Italy's first Himalayan cedar. Admission is a paid ticket, and worth it.
